_comment: Curated input for import.mjs. Real-world facts (official name, coordinates, address, opening year, exterior photo) are fetched live from Wikidata/Wikimedia Commons by QID. Descriptions, star ratings, amenities, rooms and base prices are FareLock demo data written by hand.

hotels.name: The Plaza
hotels.description: A French Renaissance château on Fifth Avenue at Central Park South, opened in 1907 and now a National Historic Landmark. Rooms look out over the park or the avenue, and the lobby still feels like the city's front parlour.
rooms: A quiet courtyard-facing room with a king bed, writing desk and marble bathroom.
Tall windows framing Central Park, a king bed and a reading chair.
Separate living room, dining table for four and a soaking tub.

hotels.name: The Algonquin Hotel
hotels.description: A Midtown institution on West 44th Street, once home to the Round Table of writers and critics. The lobby is made for lingering, a few minutes' walk from the Broadway theatres.
rooms: Compact and well considered, with a queen bed and city views.
A king bed, armchair and space to spread out after the theatre.
Living area with a bookcase of Round Table-era titles.

hotels.name: Hôtel Lutetia
hotels.description: The only grand palace hotel on the Left Bank, opened in 1910 on Boulevard Raspail facing the Square Boucicaut. Its Art Nouveau façade gives way to quiet rooms in Saint-Germain-des-Prés.
rooms: Soft greys and walnut, a king bed and Left Bank rooftops outside.
More space, a sofa by the window and a deep bathtub.
A separate sitting area with views towards the Eiffel Tower.

hotels.name: Hôtel Raphael
hotels.description: A family-run hotel from 1925 on Avenue Kléber, a short walk from the Arc de Triomphe. Expect wood panelling, antique furniture and a rooftop terrace overlooking the city.
rooms: Period furniture, a queen bed and a courtyard view.
Larger, with a king bed and views along Avenue Kléber.
A private terrace with Paris rooftops in every direction.

hotels.name: Pestana Palace Lisboa
hotels.description: A restored early-twentieth-century palace set in its own gardens in Alto de Santo Amaro, above the Tagus. Rooms sit in the palace and its newer wings around a garden pool.
rooms: Overlooking the gardens, with a king bed and balcony.
More room to unwind and a marble bathroom with bathtub.
In the historic palace, with painted ceilings and a salon.

hotels.name: Bairro Alto Hotel
hotels.description: An eighteenth-century building on Praça Luís de Camões, where Chiado meets Bairro Alto. The rooftop terrace looks over the river, and the trams run past the front door.
rooms: Calm and light, with a queen bed and a view of the square.
Tagus views and a king bed.
Corner suite with a living room and two balconies.

hotels.name: The Westin Miyako Kyoto
hotels.description: Founded in 1900 on the forested slopes of Higashiyama, a short walk from Nanzen-ji and the Philosopher's Path. Rooms look across the city or into the hotel's own gardens.
rooms: Two beds, light timber and views over the city.
A king bed facing the gardens.
Tatami living room, futon or bed, and a cypress bath.

hotels.name: Hyatt Regency Kyoto
hotels.description: Across the street from Sanjūsangen-dō temple in Higashiyama, opened in 2006. Kyoto textiles and woodwork set the tone, and Gion is a short walk north.
rooms: Kimono-fabric headboard and a king bed.
Two double beds and a deep soaking tub.
Separate lounge and dining area for longer stays.

hotels.name: Hilton Cape Town City Centre
hotels.address: 126 Buitengracht Street, Cape Town City Centre, 8001
hotels.description: On Buitengracht Street in the City Bowl, opened in 2011, with Table Mountain behind and the colourful houses of Bo-Kaap next door. The V&A Waterfront is ten minutes away.
rooms: A king bed and city or mountain views.
Higher floors and access to the executive lounge.
Corner suite with a separate lounge facing the mountain.

hotels.name: Gran Hotel Ciudad de México
hotels.address: Avenida 16 de Septiembre 82, Centro Histórico, 06000 Ciudad de México
hotels.description: Steps from the Zócalo in the Centro Histórico, under a famous Art Nouveau stained-glass canopy. The terrace restaurant looks across the square to the cathedral.
rooms: Classic furnishings and a queen bed.
A king bed and views over the historic centre.
Balcony suite overlooking the Zócalo and the cathedral.
